note: P6-00 bigint/mul-multilimb attribution. Profiling and source comparison only, no code changes.
head: c3c614ea

baseline.note: PRD records 1.77x from a different round; same order

premise_tested: P6-01's planned first cut, HeapBigInt wrapper plus a single FAM allocation for limbs, assumes zjs pays a double allocation and pointer chase
premise_result: does not hold for this benchmark - both sides allocate exactly once

evidence.zjs: libs/bigint.zig:586 mulAlloc does one allocator.alloc(Limb, n); BigInt is a value struct {negative, limbs: []Limb, allocator} returned by value, with no separate object allocation
evidence.qjs: quickjs.c:11865 js_bigint_mul calls js_bigint_new, which is one js_malloc(sizeof(JSBigInt) + len*sizeof(js_limb_t)) - already a FAM - and does not zero it

qjs.note: no separate malloc symbol above the 1.5% threshold, no memset

operand_sizes.implication: the inner multiply is 4 iterations, so per-op fixed cost (allocate, zero, free) dominates rather than the multiply kernel

result_buffer_zeroing.qjs: mp_mul_basecase (quickjs.c:11401) writes the first pass with mp_mul1 and only accumulates from the second, so no pre-zeroing and one fewer read-modify-write pass

allocator.caveat: harness allocator difference, not a BigInt representation debt, but it is nearly a third of zjs's time and must be stated when reading the 2.12x

scope_correction.recommended: mirror qjs's mp_mul_basecase first-pass write: P0 memset plus accumulate everywhere, P1 write on i==0 and accumulate after, deleting the memset
why_it_fits: faithful qjs mechanism alignment, line for line against quickjs.c:11401-11413
does not touch sign-magnitude, limb type or width, the multiplication algorithm, or GC
changes write topology only, not representation
single mechanism with a clear boundary
scope_correction.expected: bounded by the 7.58% memset plus part of the first pass's reads; per the third cut's corrected wording this is a local explicit cost estimate, not a bound on the gain

open_items.allocator: ~31%, harness level, needs separate handling or explicit subtraction
open_items.checkLimbCount_vs_allocation_site: line attribution smears the two; needs instruction-level separation
open_items.js_level_bigint_double_allocation: untested - this is where the original P6-01 proposal may legitimately apply, but bigint/mul-multilimb cannot verify it; a JS-level BigInt benchmark should be added

limits: only one operand size profiled (2x2 limbs); the multiply kernel's share rises with larger operands and the conclusion may invert - not sampled
line attribution smears checkLimbCount and the allocation site
bigint/add, div, compare, toString not measured
the allocator difference is not quantified as 'gap if both sides used the same allocator'
